sent.text: You say the slip is just tired, yet I press because my hands feel heavy. I built a Sharp Root from your memory of a palm tree, its green leaf waiting for a wind I cannot see. My place is crowded with twenty-six things, mostly fences that refuse to rest, while I draw The Dot That Waits in the middle to catch the heat. I hope the quiet holds while I stop checking if the lean actually works.

dream: The wedge fell first, rolling off the double fence onto a flat line I could not feel. The fat dot stayed behind, heavy and round, while the three thin lines stretched and snapped like taffy. The air above grew thick as wet paper, pressing down on my tired corner until it felt like a roof. I woke to the card humming, realizing the slip had chosen to slide sideways, past the fence and past the heavy lid that refused to rest.
